content: The cost of a thing is the amount of what I will call life which is required to be exchanged for it.
author: Henry David Thoreau
story:
Seeking to escape the frantic consumerism and quiet desperation of 19th-century industrial society, Thoreau built a modest cabin with his own hands on Emerson's land at Walden Pond. Living for two years on minimal expenses, he stripped life down to its absolute essentials to discover what life had to teach, famously preferring solitary simplicity over hollow material prosperity.

This insight points directly back to the quiet center of being. Henry David Thoreau observed that while the mind perpetually scatters itself into past regrets and future anxieties, peace is only ever discovered by anchoring attention in the immediate truth of this moment.
reflectionPrompt: Where can you bring full, undistracted presence into an ordinary routine or conversation today?
